stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, stating the argument the questions evaluate.
stimulus.text: A historian argues that the Columbian Exchange was an exchange of goods between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres that spread prosperity to people on both sides of the Atlantic.

stem: Some historians say syphilis sailed east from the Americas to Europe, while others say it was already in Europe before 1492. What does this disagreement best show about the Columbian Exchange?

options.misconception: Smallpox, measles, and influenza moved west; the directions were mixed, not one-way.
options.text: Every disease in the Exchange moved in only one direction, from west to east.
The origin of syphilis is still debated, so historians qualify claims about it.

options.misconception: One debated disease does not balance the epidemics that devastated the Americas.
options.text: Syphilis proves that the Exchange harmed Europe as much as the Americas.

options.misconception: The origin of syphilis is still debated; nothing here is settled.
options.text: Historians have settled that no disease ever crossed from the Americas to Europe.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
